extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level, multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. It contains 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected by over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in relevant majors. Annotators collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, created new questions when necessary, followed copyright/licensing rules, and were advised to choose questions without immediately available answers. Quality control included duplicate detection and author review, format/typo checking, and author-assigned difficulty categorization, with very easy items removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data quality was analyzed through duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review of suspected duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and difficulty categorization; the paper also reports 2% annotation error in an error analysis of 150 GPT-4V errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college/university students, including co-authors, from various disciplines/majors and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the dataset may contain biases from manual curation, and that models may be biased toward text over visual inputs when evaluated on the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include possible bias from manual curation, incomplete coverage for testing Expert AGI, weak mapping to real-world expert performance, and poor model generalization on less common image types. The benchmark is not sufficient by itself as a test for Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is framed as socially important for monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled human labor, creating risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level, expert-oriented multimodal understanding and reasoning. It includes a few-shot development set, a validation set for hyperparameter selection, and a test set; experiments are primarily conducted in zero-shot settings, with some few-shot results also reported.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to remove duplicates, format and typo checking with corrections, and filtering out about 10% of very easy problems that did not meet design criteria.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: "we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary... The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations... the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers"; "we perform two steps of data cleaning... lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels"

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: "lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors"; "distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking"; "the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels"; "The remaining errors include... Annotation Error (2%)"

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: "50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects"; "we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators"

rai:dataBiases.evidence: "MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases"; "Additionally, GPT-4V often exhibits a bias towards text, prioritizing textual information over visual inputs"

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI"; "MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI"; "there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults'"; "This indicates that the existing models are generalizing poorly towards these image types."

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: "starting to achieve 'the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor' for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI."

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning."; "The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions."; "Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting"

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy... are excluded from the benchmark.”
